subject: Service penalty framework and termination language — Altara Health
messages:
From: Matt Collins <matt.collins@altarahealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@altarahealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Service penalty framework and termination language — Altara Health

Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Altara is excited about the integration path. Before we move the procurement package to our legal team, procurement is requesting explicit penalty and exit language in the SLA beyond standard service credits. High level asks from our side:

- Fee-at-risk: a reserve of fees equal to 3 months' committed spend held as a "fee at risk" that can be drawn in defined breach events.
- Liquidated damages: a formula for per-incident damages for P1 outages (we suggested 5% of monthly committed fees per P1 after the first in a 30-day window).
- Early termination right: Altara requires a termination right for repeated material SLA breaches (we proposed termination after 3 P1s in any rolling 90-day period, no cure).

I attached a redlined SLA appendix that shows our preferred language and examples. Procurement needs confirmation of whether Redwood can accept — or if not, what counterproposal will be put forward.

Appreciate a concrete response this week.

Thanks,
Matt Collins
Head of IT Procurement
Altara Health

Attachment: SLA_Appendix_Altara_Request.pdf (pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Collins <matt.collins@altarahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service penalty framework and termination language — Altara Health

Matt —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I took this to legal and our commercial team this morning; quick summary and a constructive path forward:

1) Principle: Redwood is aligned on strong operational accountability, but we avoid indemnity-style holdbacks that are uncapped or automatic termination triggers without cure. We can offer a graduated construct that balances Altara's need for meaningful recourse with Redwood's ability to deliver and remediate.

2) Counterproposal (high level):
  - Fee-holdback: we can agree to a temporary holdback equal to 25% of one month of committed fees (not 3 months), released monthly subject to no material breaches in the prior window; releases and draws to be governed by a short appendix.
  - Liquidated damages: we propose service credits that escalate by severity and recurrence; if Altara prefers cash remedies, we can offer a capped LD schedule equal to up to 50% of one month's committed fees per quarter (explicit cap and math in appendix).
  - Termination: rather than an automatic termination after N P1s, Redwood will agree to a termination right that requires: (a) at least 3 P1s in a rolling 90-day window, (b) availability of root cause/incident reports and a 7-day cure period, and (c) an independent joint incident review for persistent failures. This gives both sides a path to remediation prior to exit.

3) Caps and timelines: we will add a quarterly cap on cash exposure and require good-faith remediation steps. We also propose a joint operational playbook (runbook) that defines severity, detection, and mitigation timelines.

I attached our proposed SLA appendix showing the numeric examples above. If Altara can accept the cure + joint review and the capped exposure, I think we can keep this in commercial terms rather than raising to exec/legal for exceptions.

If procurement needs a formal redline, I'll have our commercial counsel (Lauren) send a drafted appendix with exact wording and DocuSign link.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Appendix_Altara_Proposal.pdf (pdf)

From: SaaS Procurement <procure@altarahealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Matt Collins <matt.collins@altarahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service penalty framework and termination language — Altara Health

Mateo,

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifying points from procurement/legal:

- The 25% of one month holdback is materially lower than Altara's standard. We need 2 months' worth of committed spend (not 3 months, but more than 1 month) as an escrowed protection for regulated workloads.
- The cure window: 7 days is aggressive for us; our counsel prefers a 72-hour immediate mitigation plus a 30-day remediation period before termination can be exercised.
- The cap: Altara is open to a capped cash remedy, but the cap must be sufficient to cover repeated outages without leaving residual unrecoverable business impact.

We are not trying to be punitive, but our risk committee requires a stronger safety net in the first year of deployment. Please ask Redwood commercial/legal to provide: specific dollar examples (we've included committed spend numbers in the attached procurement matrix) and whether Redwood can accept an escrow mechanism or a restricted escrow account held by an agreed third party.

If Redwood can provide draft contract language with dollarized examples and an escrow mechanism alternative, procurement will fast-track the SOW approval.

Procurement will review Lauren's draft if she can share it by Monday.

Procurement (on behalf of Altara)
Attachment: procurement_matrix_altara.xlsx (referenced)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Collins <matt.collins@altarahealth.com>, procure@altarahealth.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service penalty framework and termination language — Altara Health

Matt / Procurement team —

Appreciate the clarity and the procurement matrix. Attached is Redwood's formal counter-draft that attempts to bridge both parties' objectives. Key points (plain language):

- Fee holdback: Redwood can agree to a 2-month restricted holdback of committed fees for the first 12 months, held in a restricted account. Access to that balance is governed by defined draw events (P1s that meet the severity threshold and follow joint incident confirmation). Any unused holdback will be released at the anniversary.

- Cure & remediation: For each qualifying P1, Redwood will commit to: an immediate mitigation plan (target: within 72 hours), a root-cause report within 10 business days, and a remediation plan with timelines. Termination may be exercised only after at least 3 qualifying P1s in a rolling 90-day window and after the remediation process (30-day remediation window) plus a joint incident review. This preserves a remediation-first approach while still allowing Altara an exit path for repeated failures.

- Liquidated damages vs credits: We propose a hybrid: first occurrence = service credits; repeated occurrences = cash draw from the holdback up to a per-quarter cap equal to 1.5x monthly committed fees. Total annual cash exposure is capped at 3x monthly committed fees.

- Governance: we agree to a quarterly SLA review with Altara's ops leader and a shared incident dashboard.

If this addresses procurement's control requirements, we'll prepare a DocuSign envelope with the SLA appendix and escrow instructions for review. If procurement wants a different trustee for the restricted account, please propose the bank/legal custodian.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the appendix Monday.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: DocuSign_Altara_SLA_Link.txt (link to envelope)
